fichas.title: Hospital Supply Area
fichas.summary: Commercial and technical supplies enter through a separate service building or a neutral basement supply and waste-disposal level. Delivery access should be separated from the main entrance and stretcher arrivals; locating delivery and waste areas to the north is described as ideal. Routes should limit interaction with care and treatment traffic. The area may cause noise and odour nuisance, and supply and waste services are increasingly centralised or outsourced.

fichas.title: Sterile Goods Supply
fichas.summary: The central sterile store should be near the surgical department and is organised by the flow of materials through acceptance, pre-cleaning, washing, sterilisation, packing and sterile storage. It prepares instruments for hospital use. The text identifies surgery and intensive-care departments as major users and notes that the number of sterilisers depends on hospital and surgical-department size.
uses: Store sterile goods for hospital use

fichas.title: Pharmaceutical Supply: Pharmacy and Dispensary
fichas.summary: Medium-sized and large hospitals may have a pharmacy that stores formulations and produces drugs under a qualified pharmacist. Required spaces may include a dispensary, materials room, drug store, laboratory and issue desk, with additional stores or rooms as needed. The pharmacy should have a short route to lifts and pneumatic post; fire-hazardous substances, acids and narcotics require secure construction. Hospitals without a full pharmacy may issue medicines requiring approval through a dispensary, with work and dispensing rooms directly accessible from the circulation corridor and adjacent medicine stores.

fichas.title: Bed Preparation
fichas.summary: Used beds and mattresses are normally disinfected by spray-and-wipe methods in the ward or room. Central bed processing that moves large numbers of beds through the building, with associated mechanical wear and wetting, is described as no longer necessary. Separate mattress disinfection in the basement may be provided, possibly combined with a bed repair room.
uses: Store clean and unclean bedding separately
